Expr.description:
A formula in the small, safe expression language.

Grammar (evaluated only by the engine, never by `eval`):   literals      12  0.5  "text"  true  false   operators     + - * /  ( )  = != > >= < <=  AND OR NOT   functions     IF(c,a,b)  MIN(a,b,..)  MAX(a,b,..)  ROUND(x,step)  CEIL(x,step)                 FLOOR(x,step)  ABS(x)  SQRT(x)  PI()  COALESCE(a,b,..)                 UNDER(term, "concrete")   true if a dictionary term is that term or beneath it   variables     any MeasuredField           e.g. net_area, thickness, length                 props["Pset_WallCommon.FireRating"]                 p.<param>                   e.g. p.opening_threshold                 src.<field> / src.qty       (derived rules only: the source element / line)   aggregates    SUM | COUNT | MIN | MAX | AVG over a collection, with optional WHERE:                   SUM(openings.area WHERE area > p.opening_threshold)                   SUM(layers.volume WHERE material = "concrete")                   COUNT(openings WHERE kind = "door")                   SUM(faces.net_area WHERE side = "a")                 collections: openings, layers, faces, children

RuleSection.description: A group of questions in the settings questionnaire, in display order.

family.description: Informative; also lets the editor offer only valid quantity kinds.

match.description: Which elements (or parts) this rule takes.

parts.description: Elements that are parts of an aggregate (a roof's slab, a stair's flights and railings) are skipped by default when some enabled rule measures the parent, to avoid counting twice. "include" measures them anyway (e.g. stair railings).

partFilter.description: Filter applied after breakdown, e.g. only layers with material = "plasterboard".

factor.description: Multiplier, e.g. allowance or overlap factor. Default 1.

minimum.description: Minimum chargeable quantity per element or per line.

lineKey.description: What splits elements into separate lines (same key = summed together).

claims.description: Double-counting guard. Each element may be claimed once per claim name (e.g. "structure", "finish_side_a"). Two rules claiming the same name on the same element is a pre-flight warning.

tags.description: Free labels used by classification maps and grouping.

enabled.description: Disable without deleting (useful in derived rule sets).

MeasuredField.description: Numeric fields rules may use as variables in formulas, selectors and bands. Written out explicitly so the JSON Schema (for the Python engine) can list them; the check below fails to compile if this list drifts from MeasuredElement.

Scalar.description:
ParsedModel — the reusable JSON produced from one IFC file (one model version).

Layer 1 of 2:   ParsedModel       faithful snapshot of the IFC. No decisions, no dictionary,                     no adopted quantities. Reused by the rules pipeline, the 3D                     viewer, revision comparison, review questions and federation.   MeasuredElement   (measured.ts) derived FROM this, with names normalised and                     quantities adopted. Cheap to recompute; this layer is not.

Conventions   - Ids are IFC GlobalIds wherever the IFC has one (stable across versions,     used to match elements between revisions). Catalogue entries without a     GlobalId (materials, layer sets) get a deterministic id "mat:<step id>".   - All lengths, areas, volumes are converted to SI (m, m2, m3). The original     unit is recorded in `header.units`.   - Coordinates are world coordinates of the file (before any federation     alignment, which is a separate step).   - Heavy geometry (meshes) is NOT in this JSON. Elements point into a     separate geometry store (e.g. a .glb with one node per GlobalId).
